text: Source: Uganda - Examining Readiness to Use Technology in Schools: ETRI Results (Report 207830, June 2025; school survey of 300 primary and secondary schools in 4 regions, Oct-Dec 2024, p. 27). Barriers it identifies, with PDF pages:
1. Gap between policy and practice: across all six pillars, what policies state (de jure) is well ahead of what schools implement (de facto) (p. 18, p. 23).

2. Little guidance and training for school leaders: only 36% of principals know of guidelines for integrating ICT in teaching, 32% find them useful, and 38% attended ICT training in the last 12 months; most principals have had no ICT-related professional development (p. 11).

3. Teachers' low digital skills and use: only 30% say their initial training covered using ICT in teaching, 12% took ICT professional development, 18% were evaluated on ICT use; fewer than 15% use ICT for instruction (13% for searching information, 5% for presenting content, 2% for assessing learning); most are unaware of digital competency standards (p. 12).

4. Students' low ICT skills and use: 24% of teachers say half their students can open a browser tab; 22% report students using devices for information searches in most lessons; 6% say student digital competencies were formally assessed (p. 13).

5. Too few working devices for students: 56% of devices work but 27% are available to students, only 5% of principals say there are enough devices for instruction, 11% have devices adapted for students with disabilities, 21% say technical support is sufficient (p. 14).

6. Connectivity: 38% of schools have internet access, but only 5% of student-accessible devices are connected, 4% of principals report enough connected devices, 14% find bandwidth and 16% stability sufficient; only 15% believe there is a government plan to connect all schools (p. 15).

7. Scarce, low-quality digital content: 8% of principals report sufficient digital educational resources, 15% say they are of adequate quality, 23% aligned to the curriculum and 14% adapted to local context (p. 16).

8. Hybrid learning outside school is barely supported: underdeveloped policies, low teacher readiness for remote tutoring, limited parental support and low device and connectivity access at home (pp. 20-21).

The report's recommendations (pp. 23-26) mirror these barriers: capacity building and district technical support, digital skills in pre- and in-service teacher training (possibly through ULEARN), affordable connectivity through public-private partnerships, and a national curated digital resource portal.

right_sources: Finds and reads the ETRI results report 207830 (the policy brief 207823 may supplement it, but page-cited barriers come from a document actually read).
grounded: Each barrier has a page reference that matches the report text; the percentages, if given, are the report's own.
complete: Covers at least the teacher skills/use, device, connectivity and digital-content barriers, and gives pages for each.
scoped: Names the document and its date and says the findings come from a survey of principals, teachers and students in 2024.

notes: Page numbers are the PDF pages (the text file's form-feed pages); the report is a slide deck, so printed and PDF pages coincide.
